digest.headline: Saudi Aramco posted a third-quarter profit of $36.25bn as US stock futures climbed ahead of congressional midterms.

lede.b: Stock futures in the United States climbed as crude oil prices extended recent declines. Stock futures are contracts to buy or sell shares at a set price on a future date. This happened ahead of the congressional midterms. Wall Street indices attempted a recovery after hitting three-month lows. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 eminis rose in early trading while the Dow Jones fell nearly 200 points.
lede.i: US stock futures advanced as crude oil prices extended recent declines ahead of the congressional midterms. Wall Street indices attempted a recovery after hitting three-month lows. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 eminis rose in early trading while the Dow Jones fell nearly 200 points. These moves occurred as artificial intelligence earnings failed to meet market expectations.
lede.a: US stock futures climbed alongside declining crude oil prices ahead of the congressional midterms. Wall Street indices attempted a recovery after touching three-month lows, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 eminis rising in early trading while the Dow Jones dropped nearly 200 points. Concurrently, the Nasdaq-100 entered a correction phase as artificial intelligence earnings missed market expectations and Hamilton Lane reported third-quarter sales below analyst estimates.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Stock futures rise as US midterm elections begin

stories.t: Stock Futures Rise Amid Declining Oil Prices and Midterm Elections
stories.b: Stock futures are financial contracts that let buyers trade shares at a set price later. Wall Street futures rose as oil prices dropped and voters headed to the polls for the US midterm elections. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices opened higher following earlier declines. The Dow Jones fell nearly 200 points as polls began.
stories.i: Stock futures climbed as crude oil prices extended their recent declines ahead of the congressional midterms. Wall Street indices attempted a recovery after hitting three-month lows. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 eminis rose in early trading while the Dow Jones fell nearly 200 points.
stories.a: Equity index futures advanced as sliding oil prices intersected with positioning for the US midterm elections. The Nasdaq-100 attempted a technical recovery from three-month lows following a severe correction driven by disappointing artificial intelligence sector earnings. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones pulled back nearly 200 points at the opening bell.

stories.t: Nasdaq-100 Faces Correction Pressure as Earnings Disappoint
stories.b: The Nasdaq-100 is a stock market index that tracks one hundred of the largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange, heavily weighted toward technology firms. This index entered a correction, which means a drop of 10% or more from recent highs, because artificial intelligence earnings reports were not good enough for investors. Hamilton Lane also reported sales below analyst expectations for the third quarter of 2026.
stories.i: The Nasdaq-100 entered a correction phase after artificial intelligence earnings failed to meet market expectations. Hamilton Lane reported third-quarter sales that fell below analyst estimates. ProShares Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF declared a monthly distribution of $0.2313.
stories.a: The Nasdaq-100 re-entered correction territory as artificial intelligence sector earnings were deemed inadequate by institutional participants. Hamilton Lane reported third-quarter CY2026 sales below consensus estimates. Concurrently, the ProShares Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF declared a monthly distribution of $0.2313.

politics.b: The United States held midterm elections on November 3, 2026. Voters cast ballots for congressional seats and local offices while markets reacted to the political shift. Historical data shows that midterm elections have triggered S&P 500 gains 100% of the time.
politics.i: US midterm elections began on November 3, 2026, with investors assessing the potential market impact of a Democratic sweep. Historical records indicate that midterm election cycles have consistently preceded S&P 500 gains. Meanwhile, the average stock outperformed the S&P 500 by the widest margin since 2009.
politics.a: US midterm voting commenced on November 3, 2026, prompting analysis regarding the asset price implications of a Democratic sweep versus divided government outcomes. Historical seasonality data shows S&P 500 gains following every historical midterm event. Breadth metrics showed the average stock outperforming the S&P 500 by the most since 2009.

timeline: Hamilton Lane reported third-quarter CY2026 sales below analyst estimates.
ProShares Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF declared a monthly distribution of $0.2313.
US midterm elections began as Wall Street futures rose and the Dow fell nearly 200 points.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank rate expectations and credit union exploration

stories.t: Bank of England Faces Rate Hike Expectations
stories.b: The Bank of England is the group that sets borrowing costs for the nation. This institution is expected to raise its main interest rate. Interest is the extra money paid back on a loan. The Bank of England will join other global banks in making this move.
stories.i: The Bank of England is expected to join international peers in lifting its benchmark interest rate. Higher central bank rates aim to curb rising prices across the economy. Financial markets have adjusted their pricing to reflect this anticipated policy tightening by the Monetary Policy Committee.
stories.a: The Bank of England faces market pricing consistent with a normalization cycle alongside global counterparts. Anticipation of higher policy rates alters yield curves and shifts front-end pricing. The validity of this market read depends on persistence in domestic price pressures holding above target.

stories.t: Credit Union Reforms Explored
stories.b: The Bank of England and the Prudential Regulation Authority are studying credit unions. Credit unions are smaller member-owned financial cooperatives that hold consumer savings and offer loans. Officials want to see how these groups can grow and bring new ideas to the financial sector.
stories.i: The Bank of England and the Prudential Regulation Authority are investigating potential regulatory changes for credit unions. Regulators intend to support sector growth and financial innovation through these policy adjustments. Officials aim to expand the operational scope of these cooperative lenders.
stories.a: The Bank of England and the Prudential Regulation Authority are evaluating structural reforms for the credit union sector to stimulate market competition. Regulators are targeting statutory constraints to facilitate balance sheet expansion and product innovation among mutual lenders. The transmission mechanism relies on lowering compliance barriers to enhance credit provision in underserved segments.

politics.b: Politicians faced questions about the recent national budget document. Ipsos noted that the public discussed this budget online less than in the previous two years. Observers also debated how political figures communicated spending plans.
politics.i: The national budget generated lower online public engagement compared to the prior two years, according to Ipsos data. Political figures faced scrutiny over their communication strategy surrounding the fiscal package. Critics argued that officials were vocal during the proposal stage but less responsive afterward.
politics.a: Public discourse surrounding the recent fiscal event registered lower digital volume relative to the prior two electoral cycles, per Ipsos metrics. Political friction arose regarding executive accountability for the announced tax and spending measures. Opposition figures criticized the administration's defensive posture following the legislative introduction of the budget.

timeline: Goldman Sachs lifted its forecasts for the pound sterling.

stories.b: The DAX is an index, which is a basket of big company shares. Shares are tiny slices of ownership in a business. The DAX index fell 0.63% to 25,818 points at midday. Investors remained wary ahead of elections.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen movements and leisure market expansion

stories.t: Japanese Yen Trades in Ranges Ahead of Elections
stories.b: The Japanese Yen trades against the US Dollar while investors focus on political votes. Currencies change value compared to each other every day. Traders watch these shifts very closely. Range trading persists between the two currencies. The Japanese Yen weakens against the US Dollar.
stories.i: The Japanese Yen trades in narrow ranges against the US Dollar. Market participants focus heavily on the US midterm elections. The carry trade dynamics shift as traders adjust positions. Range trading persists according to updates from UOB. The Japanese Yen weakens against the US Dollar.
stories.a: The Japanese Yen maintains established technical bands against the US Dollar. US midterm elections dominate macroeconomic sentiment and near-term positioning. Cross-asset volatility remains contained as range trading persists. The Japanese Yen weakens against the US Dollar in recent sessions.

stories.t: Japan Leisure Sector Grows to 78 Trillion Yen
stories.b: Japan records higher spending on leisure activities in a recent official report. The entire leisure market scale reaches 78 trillion yen. This total represents an increase of 3.9% from the previous period. The figures appear in the Leisure White Paper 2026. Consumers spend more money on entertainment and free time.
stories.i: Japan registers expansion in its domestic service and entertainment sectors. The leisure market scale climbs 3.9% to 78 trillion yen in 2025. The Leisure White Paper 2026 details these annual consumption metrics. Consumer spending drives this notable sectoral growth. The total market valuation reaches 78 trillion yen.
stories.a: Japan documents broad consumer recovery reflected in annual recreational spending data. The Leisure White Paper 2026 places total market scale at 78 trillion yen. This aggregate represents a 3.9% year-on-year expansion. Commercial leisure turnover achieves 78 trillion yen across the measured annual cycle.

China.label: China
China.sub: Crown New Materials debuts and currency measures shape markets

stories.t: Crown New Materials Opens on Shenzhen Stock Exchange
stories.b: Crown New Materials is a company. It just started trading its shares on the stock market in Shenzhen. Shares are tiny slices of ownership in a business. The opening market capitalization reached $3.7bn. Market capitalization is the total value of all those slices combined.
stories.i: Crown New Materials opened its debut trading session on the Shenzhen exchange. The initial market capitalization reached $3.7bn. This valuation reflects the total equity value priced by public investors at launch.
stories.a: Crown New Materials commenced public trading on the Shenzhen venue with a capitalization print of $3.7bn. The primary listing adds fresh equity supply to the domestic index. Initial pricing implies strong early demand relative to prevailing book-building expectations.

stories.t: Reserve Requirement Hike Aims to Slow Yuan Rise
stories.b: The central bank is the main bank that runs a country's money system. It raised a rule called the reserve requirement. This rule tells regular banks to keep more money locked up and lend out less. The goal is to slow down how fast the local money, the yuan, gets stronger.
stories.i: Authorities implemented a reserve requirement hike to temper the currency's rapid appreciation. Higher reserve ratios compel lenders to hold more idle capital, restricting domestic liquidity expansion. This policy lever seeks to moderate the pace of the yuan's advance against major peers.
stories.a: Policymakers adjusted the reserve requirement ratio to stem the velocity of the yuan's inflation-adjusted strength. The monetary tightening tool curtails commercial bank lending capacity by increasing mandatory vault cash. Market participants now reprice forward trajectory assumptions following the intervention.

politics.b: Sanxing New Materials is facing an official investigation by the securities regulator. The company reported a larger loss of 62.17m yuan for the first three quarters.
politics.i: Sanxing New Materials encountered a formal probe by the CSRC. The regulatory scrutiny coincides with an expansion of losses to 62.17m yuan across the first three quarters.
politics.a: Regulatory intervention from the CSRC targets Sanxing New Materials amid deteriorating financial disclosures. The enterprise reported an expanded net loss of 62.17m yuan for the nine-month period ending in the third quarter.

timeline: Crown New Materials lists on the Shenzhen exchange with a $3.7bn market capitalization.
Sanxing New Materials reports a widened nine-month loss of 62.17m yuan and faces a CSRC probe.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity auctions, NSE earnings, and rupee gains

stories.t: NSE Reports Q2 Earnings and Trading Hour Expansion
stories.b: The National Stock Exchange made ₹2,578 crore in net profit for the second quarter of financial year 27. This is a 23% increase compared to last year. Its revenue also grew by 10.6%. Meanwhile, NSEIX extended its trading schedule to 23.5 hours to provide near round-the-clock access.
stories.i: The National Stock Exchange posted a net profit of ₹2,578 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 23% year-on-year rise alongside a 10.6% revenue increase. Concurrently, NSEIX extended its operating hours to 23.5 hours daily. These updates precede the fourth straight session of market gains on Dalal Street.
stories.a: The National Stock Exchange printed a net profit of ₹2,578 crore for Q2FY27 on 10.6% revenue growth. NSEIX concurrently expanded its operational window to 23.5 hours to capture extended liquidity flows. Equities extended a pre-Diwali rally for a fourth consecutive session.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Schedules Variable Rate Reverse Repo Auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India announced a Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction for November 04, 2026. A reverse repo is an auction where the central bank borrows money from commercial banks to manage cash levels in the financial system. This particular auction will absorb ₹50,000 crore from the banking system for a single day. The funds will return to the market on November 05, 2026.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction for November 04, 2026, to manage prevailing liquidity conditions. The central bank notified a total amount of ₹50,000 crore for a single-day tenor. Bidding runs from 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM, with the reversal scheduled for November 05, 2026.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction for November 04, 2026, to drain system liquidity. The central bank set a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore with a 1-day tenor. The auction window operates from 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM ahead of the reversal date on November 05, 2026.

stories.t: State Government Securities Results and Survey Launches
stories.src: Reserve Bank of India · India markets
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India published auction results for State Government Securities covering Andhra Pradesh and Delhi. Andhra Pradesh raised money across two tenors at yields of 8.0089% and 8.1463%. Delhi raised funds through a re-issue with a 7.8890% yield. Separately, the central bank launched its November 2026 rounds of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households, Urban Consumer Confidence Survey, and Rural Consumer Confidence Survey across 19 cities.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India released auction results for State Government Securities where Andhra Pradesh issued debt at cut-off yields of 8.0089% and 8.1463%, and Delhi issued at 7.8890%. In parallel, the central bank initiated the November 2026 rounds of its urban and rural consumer confidence surveys alongside household inflation expectations surveys across 19 cities. Additionally, the central bank eased reporting norms for small service exporters and importers.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India accepted ₹1,000 crore and ₹2,000 crore for Andhra Pradesh state development loans at cut-off yields of 8.0089% and 8.1463%, alongside Delhi's ₹500 crore issuance at 7.8890%. The central bank concurrently deployed the November 2026 rounds of its inflation expectations and consumer confidence surveys across 19 urban and rural centers. Regulatory reporting requirements were simultaneously relaxed for small service exporters and importers.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of India launched new household surveys across 19 cities to check consumer sentiment and price expectations. State governments also raised money through debt auctions.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India launched the November 2026 rounds of its urban and rural consumer confidence surveys and household inflation expectations across 19 cities. State governments raised funds through the issuance of state development loans.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of India initiated its recurring urban and rural consumer confidence surveys alongside household inflation expectations across 19 cities. State governments successfully executed debt re-issues through the central bank's auction mechanism.

timeline: State Government Securities auction held and November surveys launched

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Brazil growth forecasts rise after election and rates stall

stories.t: Economists adjust forecasts following election outcome
stories.b: Economists in Brazil raised their forecasts for price rises. Price rises mean things cost more over time. They also raised predictions for borrowing costs. These changes followed the reelection of Lula. Market uncertainty slowed down plans for further reductions in the Selic interest rate.
stories.i: Brazilian economists raised their inflation and rate forecasts following the reelection of Lula. Market turmoil dimmed prospects for further Selic rate cuts. These adjustments reflect shifting expectations across domestic financial markets.
stories.a: Forecasters marked up inflation and terminal rate projections following the Lula reelection. Sustained market volatility impaired the transmission mechanism for further Selic rate reductions. Pricing now implies a prolonged pause in monetary easing.

stories.t: Petrobras secures safety deal as analysts adjust targets
stories.src: Riviera Maritime Media · TradingView · World Oil
stories.b: Oceanity signed a contract with Petrobras for a fast oil spill response vessel. TradingView adjusted its 12-month price target for Petrobras stock down to $23.67. Baker Hughes also established a global hub network for mature oil and gas fields.
stories.i: Oceanity signed an agreement with Petrobras for an oil spill response vessel. TradingView cut its Petrobras stock price target to $23.67, which implies a 12% upside. Baker Hughes launched a global hub network to support mature oil and gas fields.
stories.a: Oceanity finalized a contract with Petrobras for an additional fast oil spill response vessel. TradingView revised the 12-month price target for Petrobras down to $23.67, implying a 12% upside. Baker Hughes deployed a global hub network targeting mature field production assets.

politics.b: Lula won reelection in Brazil. Economists updated their financial predictions following the political outcome. Markets reacted with uncertainty to the change.
politics.i: Lula secured reelection in Brazil. The political result prompted economists to adjust their inflation and rate projections. Financial markets responded with increased volatility.
politics.a: The reelection of Lula triggered upward revisions to macroeconomic forecasts. Market participants recalibrated risk premiums following the political outcome. Analysts adjusted rate expectations accordingly.

timeline: Baker Hughes launched a global hub network for mature oil and gas fields.
Brazil economists raised inflation and rate forecasts after Lula reelection.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Saudi Aramco Q3 profit figures and pipeline targets

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Posts Third-Quarter Profits
stories.src: houseofsaud.com · Agência de Notícias Brasil-Árabe - ANBA
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is a massive company that sells oil. It made $36.25bn in profit during the third quarter. Profit is the money left over after paying all business costs. This huge amount came even though oil prices went up and down.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco reported a third-quarter profit of $36.25bn. Higher oil prices helped drive a profit surge of 34.6%. Refining margins offset an upstream profit decline during the period.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco delivered $36.25bn in third-quarter profit, representing a 34.6% surge. Strong refining margins successfully absorbed upstream profit headwinds. Global inventory rebuilding supports forward demand expectations.

stories.t: Infrastructure and Expansion Targets Set by Aramco
stories.src: ارقام : اخبار ومعلومات سوق الأسهم السعودي - تاسي · TradeWinds News
stories.b: Saudi Aramco plans to make its East-West pipeline carry 10m barrels of oil per day by the year 2030. A barrel is a standard measure for oil volume. Gas investments should also add $15bn in cash flow by 2030.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco targets 10m bpd capacity for the East-West pipeline by 2030. Gas investments aim to generate a $15bn cash flow boost by the same year. The firm is also probing new oil export routes alongside these pipeline expansions.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco targets a 10m bpd throughput capacity on the East-West pipeline by 2030. Planned gas investments underpin a projected $15bn cash flow expansion over the same horizon. Management is actively probing alternative export routes as infrastructure scaling advances.

politics.b: The Saudi economy continues to diversify its base and strengthen its resilience according to actual budget performance data for the third quarter.
politics.i: Actual budget performance for the third quarter shows the Saudi economy continuing to diversify its base and strengthen its resilience.
politics.a: Third-quarter actual budget performance reports indicate ongoing diversification of the Saudi economic base and strengthened fiscal resilience.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira falls against the dollar and bank customers protest

stories.t: Naira Slips in Markets
stories.b: A currency is the money used in a country. The naira is the money used in Nigeria, and the dollar is used in the United States. The central bank updated exchange rates after the naira dropped in value. The naira weakened to N1,378 per dollar in the parallel market.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria updated exchange rates as the domestic currency fell against the US dollar. The naira weakened to N1,378 per dollar in the parallel market. Meanwhile, trading turnover in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market dropped below $300 million.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Nigeria adjusted official rates following downward pressure on the naira. The currency depreciated to N1,378 per dollar in parallel trading channels. Concurrently, foreign exchange market turnover contracted below $300 million, marking the lowest level since September 28.

stories.t: Bank Customers Protest Losses
stories.b: A bank is a business where people keep their money. Customers are the people who use the bank. Customers of Jaiz Bank in Nigeria held a protest. They stated they lost more than ₦100 million.
stories.i: Customers of Jaiz Bank staged a protest in Nigeria. The demonstrators claimed losses exceeding ₦100 million. Bank customers voiced their anger over the missing funds.
stories.a: Jaiz Bank customers organized a demonstration in Nigeria. Protesters asserted financial losses surpassing ₦100 million. The grievances center on disputed account balances reported by the institution's clientele.

politics.b: Shipowners asked an official named Oyeyola to clarify issues. They talked about a reported conversion to the naira. The Securities and Exchange Commission set a target of ₦750 trillion by the year 2036.
politics.i: Shipowners tasked Oyeyola with clarifying reports regarding a conversion to the naira. The Securities and Exchange Commission announced a target of ₦750 trillion for the capital market by 2036.
politics.a: Shipowners directed inquiries to Oyeyola concerning the reported conversion of funds to the naira. Meanwhile, the Securities and Exchange Commission established a capitalization target of ₦750 trillion for the Nigerian capital market by 2036.

stories.b: The Australian Dollar recovered some ground after a central bank move. A central bank is the institution that manages a country's money supply and interest rates. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised borrowing costs. ING analysts keep a year-end target of 0.7100 for the currency.
stories.i: The Australian Dollar recovered some ground following a dovish rate increase by the Reserve Bank of Australia. ING analysts maintain their year-end target of 0.7100 for the currency pairing. The central bank delivered a tightening move that markets interpreted as cautious.
